title: FrankenMotion: Part-level Human Motion Generation and Composition
summary: Learns hierarchical part/action/sequence-conditioned diffusion instead of test-time pose stitching.
method: CLIP action/part embeddings are PCA-reduced to 50 dimensions, expanded framewise and concatenated with noisy motion through an MLP; sequence and diffusion-step features are extra tokens. Unknown labels are zeroed; Beta-distributed random masking improves sparse-conditioning robustness.
conditions: Temporally aligned, potentially sparse sequence, action and seven-body-part text; FrankenStein extends existing mocap annotations using LLM reasoning.
evaluation: UniMotion, STMC and DART are adapted and retrained on FrankenStein using the same pose representation. Nine separate TMR-style evaluators assess seven parts, actions and sequences using R-Precision/M2T; realism uses FID/Diversity. Evaluations repeat 20 times with 95% confidence intervals. Annotation audit: 50 sequences, three experts.
limitations: Authors explicitly cannot generate minute-long sequences in one pass. Label audit samples only 50 sequences; learned semantic metrics do not establish contact physics.

title: Towards Decompositional Human Motion Generation with Energy-Based Diffusion Models
summary: Trains compositional scores to reconstruct holistic motion without individual-concept motion targets.
method: Frozen-VAE motion latents are denoised with summed concept-conditioned predictions (latent-aware), or decomposed cross-attention (semantic-aware). Exp uses decomposed captions; OSS splits text embeddings with orthogonality; SC adds semantic consistency against decomposed embeddings.
conditions: Exp requires decomposed text; OSS/SC infer concepts without decomposed inference prompts. DeCompML splits HumanML3D captions using GPT-4.1; default decomposition uses two concepts.
evaluation: HumanML3D-pretrained models are directly evaluated on MTT and DeCompML. Exp handles multiple-text composition; OSS/SC handle single-text multi-concept generation. DeCompML combines decomposed captions with HumanML3D test motions and uses its text-motion evaluator. MTT reports R-Precision, TMR scores, FID and transition distance.
limitations: Authors find Exp degrades for three/four text components as captions lack information. Component visualization is qualitative; it does not supply independent ground-truth primitive motions.

title: EnergyMoGen: Compositional Human Motion Generation with Energy-Based Diffusion Model in Latent Space
summary: Combines latent and text-attention energy formulations for concept conjunction and negation.
method: Classifier-free diffusion predictions implement latent-aware energy composition. Cross-attention provides semantic-aware composition and adaptive text-embedding gradient updates; Synergistic Energy Fusion reconciles the two. Main inference uses five latent vectors and 50 diffusion steps.
conditions: Multiple textual concepts, logical conjunction/negation; whole-motion latent representation rather than explicit per-frame body-part stitching.
evaluation: HumanML3D/KIT-ML evaluate ordinary text generation. MTT compares combined single text against multiple-text composition using original constituent captions. Metrics follow STMC: R-Precision, TMR-Score, FID, transition distance. CompML contains 5,000 generated pairs from random triples of STMC captions, used with HumanML3D for augmentation experiments.
limitations: Appendix J reports failure on completely novel concepts. MTT semantic/transition metrics and synthetic augmentation do not demonstrate real object-contact consistency.

title: Multi-Track Timeline Control for Text-Driven 3D Human Motion Generation
summary: Test-time spatial stitching and temporal score arithmetic operate at every diffusion step.
method: Independently denoises prompt crops; body-part assignments select explicit pose components. Adjacent crops are extended by overlap (example: 0.25 seconds); their predictions are summed and an unconditional overlap prediction subtracted before the next reverse step.
conditions: Text intervals with durations and compatible body-part assignments from GPT-3 or user. Requires explicit-pose denoisers; latent models cannot directly expose stitchable joints.
evaluation: MTT has 500 automatically constructed timelines, each three prompts over two tracks, drawn from 60 manually collected/body-part-labeled actions with matching AMASS references. Compares single-text, DiffCollage and SINC variants using semantic and realism metrics plus perceptual studies.
limitations: Authors report inherited base-model limits, unfamiliar stitched poses, compatible-part restriction and imperfect timing. Proposed late-denoising stitching schedules are future work, not evaluated capability.
